The test image shows a corn stalk with dark brown/black discoloration at a node, with the stalk appearing to break at that point. The plant is still green. This is a **stem** disease.

Stem candidates: Anthracnose, Bacterial_Stalk_Rot, Charcoal_Stalk_Rot, Common_Smut, Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma, Diplodia_Stalk_Rot, Head_Smut, Physoderma_Brown_Spot, Physoderma_Stalk_Rot, Purple_Leaf_Sheath, Stewart_S_Disease.

The black node with snapping stalk strongly suggests Physoderma_Stalk_Rot. Let me view references across top candidates.
Physoderma_Stalk_Rot ref shows dark spots on the stalk sheath area, somewhat different pattern. Let me check other candidates.
Anthracnose shows shiny black lesions on dried stalks, quite different. Let me continue checking.
Purple_Leaf_Sheath shows discrete dark spots on green sheaths, different pattern. Let me check more candidates.
This Physoderma_Stalk_Rot reference is much closer - a stalk broken at a dark node with the plant still partly green. Let me check two more candidates.

Charcoal_Stalk_Rot shows internal shredding with sclerotia, very different. The third Physoderma_Stalk_Rot reference (Corn_Disease_71.jpg) is an excellent match: a green stalk snapped at a dark, rotted node, nearly identical to the test image.

**Analysis:**
- Test image: Green corn stalk with dark brown/black discoloration concentrated at the node, stalk breaking/snapping at that node point
- Physoderma_Stalk_Rot KB description: "Black nodes at first or second node, pith rot, nodes that snap easily when pushed. Affected plants often look healthy with no visible brown spot symptoms on leaves." This matches perfectly.
- Visual match: References #2 (Corn_Disease_53) and #3 (Corn_Disease_71) both show green stalks breaking at darkened nodes, closely matching the test image
- Other candidates eliminated: Anthracnose (shiny black on dried stalks), Diplodia (fully dried/dead), Bacterial_Stalk_Rot (water-soaked mushy tissue), Purple_Leaf_Sheath (discrete spots), Charcoal_Stalk_Rot (internal shredding/sclerotia)
